clue.text: Harassment in MI6 HQ?

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation, the kind of agent Britain's MI6 runs or hunts
a station is a base or headquarters, as in a police or naval station

explanation.surface: A complaint of harassment inside the headquarters of Britain's foreign intelligence service.
explanation.walkthrough: MI6 is Britain's foreign intelligence service; the clue imagines its HQ as a base for spies, splitting the answer into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Harassment and pestering a person are both covered by this noun for persistent annoyance or abuse.

clue.text: Privilege after starter's gone to tuck into flesh in animal

indicators.note: the shortened privilege is tucked inside the word for flesh

parts.note: meat is animal flesh

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for privilege is dropped

parts.note: a perk is a privilege or fringe benefit of a job

explanation.surface: A creature is pictured tucking into meat as a reward for good behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck into' looks like eating, matching the animal picture, but here it means go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The meerkat is a small burrowing mongoose of southern Africa, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Country invested in, say, billions after revolution

indicators.note: after revolution says the hidden letters are read backwards
invested in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A nation that billions were poured into after its uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Country invested' as the definition, but 'invested in' is the hiding signal; 'Country' alone defines. AYBIL hides in 'say, billions' and turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Libya is a North African state on the Mediterranean, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Place for filming footballer is a disappointment

parts.note: a set is where a film or TV scene is shot
a back is a defending player in football

explanation.surface: A footballer acting in a film finds the experience a letdown.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback is a reverse or check to progress, which amounts to a disappointment.

clue.text: After a time, Fifties rocker's rattled

indicators.note: After places the rocker's name behind the preceding pieces

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress who loved rock and roll

explanation.surface: After a while, an old rock-and-roll fan from the 1950s gets shaken up.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys (Teds) were a 1950s British youth subculture. 'Aerated' is British slang for agitated or worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: In British informal use, getting aerated means becoming agitated or worked up, much like being rattled.

clue.text: Unidentified fool blocking work to support trendy firm

indicators.note: in a down light the following piece sits beneath and props up the first ones

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: the word for fool sits inside the word for work, blocking it

parts.note: go means work or function, as a machine does
a nit, short for nitwit, is a fool

explanation.surface: An anonymous idiot gets in the way of a job backing a fashionable company.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'to support' means sitting underneath; 'blocking' means inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone travelling incognito conceals their identity, so they go unidentified.

clue.text: Two features of tennis in another game

parts.note: a tennis match has a net across the court
a tennis match is played with a ball

explanation.surface: Two things found in tennis also turn up in a different sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team sport in which players shoot a ball through a high hoop, an example of a game.

clue.text: Basil, say, among group getting drink

indicators.note: the herb goes among, inside, the letters for group

parts.note: a set is a group
basil is an example of a herb

explanation.surface: A man named Basil joins a crowd for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basil' looks like a man's name but is the herb, with 'say' marking an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherbet is a fizzy sweet drink or the powder for one, so it fits drink.

clue.text: Best travel is arranged, needing to cover up, going to Spain

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap round, covering, the next piece
arranged says the letters of travel is are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: The best journeys are well organised, involving wrapping up warmly and heading for Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles TRAVEL IS to SERLATIV, which covers UP as S-UP-ERLATIV; E for Spain finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative means of the highest quality, so it is a synonym of best as an adjective.

clue.text: Italian staple put in apricot tart

indicators.note: put in says the letters are placed inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A basic Italian ingredient is added to an apricot tart.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft Italian whey cheese widely used in cooking, a staple of that cuisine.

clue.text: Broth nearly spilt in a repugnant way

indicators.note: spilt suggests the letters of broth nearly are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Soup nearly knocked over in a disgusting manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorrent means detestable, so the adverb describes acting in a repugnant way.

clue.text: Mention of wrinkle being genuine

indicators.note: Mention of says the word is spoken and heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a pucker is a wrinkle or crease

explanation.surface: Talk of a crease turns out to be real.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the word for a wrinkle is said the same as the Anglo-Indian word for genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pukka, from Hindi, is British informal for real or authentic, a synonym of genuine.

clue.text: Sign of the self?

parts.note: a person's own signature, with auto meaning self and graph meaning writing

explanation.surface: A philosophical question about what marks out one's own identity.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's own handwritten signature is literally a writing of the self, a self-made sign.

clue.text: The sliding in ice venue is deliberate again

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the venue word

parts.note: a rink is a venue for ice skating

indicators.note: sliding suggests the letters of the word The slip into a new order

explanation.surface: Skaters sliding about an ice rink reconsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sliding' looks like skaters on the ice but signals the shuffle of the word 'The'.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberate again is to think a matter over afresh, to reconsider a plan.

clue.text: Reveal involvement of brat with deceit about pet

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child, a brat

indicators.note: the word for deceit goes about, around, the pet

parts.note: a lie is a deceit
a cat is a typical pet

explanation.surface: A naughty child lies about the family pet, giving himself away.
explanation.definitionFit: To implicate someone is to show they are involved in a crime or wrongdoing.

clue.text: Ambition followed by inexperienced driver in the German car

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the German article

parts.note: der is a German word for the

indicators.note: followed by sets the driver's letter after the ambition

parts.note: an aim is an ambition
L stands for learner, from the L-plate shown by a driver still learning

explanation.surface: A learner driver with big dreams sits in a German car.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver displays an L-plate, so L is the learner.
explanation.definitionFit: Daimler is a car marque, so the name stands for a car.

clue.text: A large restrictive area holding soft drink for teenagers

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

indicators.note: the enclosure word holds the next letter inside

parts.note: a coop is a small cage or pen that confines animals
p, piano, is the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A big zone restricted to under-age people keeps a soft drink on hand.
explanation.walkthrough: An alcopop is a sweet, fizzy, ready-mixed alcoholic drink, so 'soft drink' is a false path: soft is P, from music.
explanation.definitionFit: These sweet fizzy premixed alcoholic drinks were criticised for appealing to teenagers.

clue.text: Put up with dirty place, home for fliers?

parts.note: to cock is to raise or put up, as in cocking an ear
a pit is a dirty, squalid place

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates a filthy house where birds live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' reads as tolerate, but 'Put up' is COCK and 'with' joins it to PIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilots sit at the controls in this cabin of an aircraft, playfully called the home of those who fly.

clue.text: Groomed European enters before finale

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: the letter for European goes inside the pieces that follow

parts.note: an end is a finale

explanation.surface: A European walks in just before the grand finale, having tidied himself up.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird that preened has tidied its feathers, so the word means groomed itself.

clue.text: Short time in Lancashire town almost producing laugh

indicators.note: the letter for time goes inside the shortened town
almost drops the last letter of the town's name

parts.note: Chorley is a market town in Lancashire, north-west England
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A brief stay in a northern English town makes someone giggle.
explanation.walkthrough: Chorley is a town in Lancashire, a county of north-west England; 'almost' trims it to CHORLE for T to go in.
explanation.definitionFit: To chortle is to laugh with gleeful chuckling, a word coined by Lewis Carroll.

clue.text: Fall of dishonourable type in action

indicators.note: the rogue goes inside the word for action

parts.note: a case is a legal action or lawsuit
a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably

explanation.surface: A scoundrel is caught in the act and tumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' is the legal sense: a case brought in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a waterfall, water falling in stages, so it means a fall.

clue.text: Volunteer, one that could be given lead?

definitions.meaning: a British slang term for a volunteer soldier of the Territorial Army

definitions.text: one that could be given lead?
definitions.meaning: a breed of dog, which is walked on a lead

explanation.surface: Someone who offers their help might be put in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve force. 'lead' reads as leadership but is a dog's leash.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserve soldier is nicknamed this, and the small hunting dog is walked on a leash.

clue.text: Unpleasant sensation is in chest possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of is in chest may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A nasty feeling in the chest, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is an irritating skin feeling, so the state of having one is an unpleasant sensation.

clue.text: Walk proudly in part of framework?

definitions.meaning: to swagger along with head high
a bar or brace in a structure that resists pressure along its length

explanation.surface: Someone parades with pride as one piece of a larger structure.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to swagger, and the noun is a supporting bar in a frame.

clue.text: Garment that's right in humorous show

indicators.note: the letter for right goes inside the show

parts.note: a skit is a short comic sketch

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing that is just right appears in a comedy sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirt is a garment hanging from the waist, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Account for former partner left in agony

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: the letter for left goes inside the word for agony

parts.note: pain is agony

explanation.surface: Someone must justify why an ex was left suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: To account for something is to give the reasons behind it, to make it clear.

clue.text: Skill I kindled in a boy, nothing less

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the shortened phrase
less says the letter for nothing is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
O, the figure zero, means nothing
taken as written
lit means kindled, set alight

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have sparked talent in a young lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing less' removes O from A BOY to leave ABY, and 'in' puts I and LIT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ability is the capacity or talent to do something well, a synonym of skill.

clue.text: One initiating rage?

parts.note: rage here means a craze or fashion, not anger, so the person starts a fad

explanation.surface: A person who sparks fury in others.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leads the way in fashion starts each new craze or vogue that others follow.
